claims.statement: The arcade merging strategy is a single per-system value: systems.merging stores a Merging discriminant (Split=0, NonMerged=1, FullNonMerged=2, Merged=3, FullMerged=4), and only SPLIT, NON_MERGED and FULL_NON_MERGED are selectable or ever written (clap MERGING_STRATEGIES plus update_system_merging); Merged/FullMerged are only handled defensively in exhaustive matches.

systems.merging determines how completion is computed: compute_system_completion selects update_split_games_completion_by_system_id for Split (roms with a parent_id are ignored), the non-merged/merged variant for NonMerged/Merged (only roms merged from a non-BIOS parent are required), and the unconditional update for FullNonMerged/FullMerged, so the same set can be Full or None purely from the stored strategy.

The GraphQL Rom::ignored resolver derives whether a merged rom is needed from the system's merging value: always ignored under Split, ignored only when its parent rom belongs to a BIOS game under NonMerged/Merged, never ignored under FullNonMerged/FullMerged.

The parent/clone and BIOS graph rebuild relies on is built by DAT import, not by rebuild: create_or_update_games resolves cloneof/romof into games.parent_id and games.bios_id in repeated passes, and create_or_update_roms resolves the Logiqx merge attribute into roms.parent_id by matching size+CRC against the clone's BIOS, its parent, and the parent's BIOS, setting roms.bios when the source is a BIOS rom.

rebuild-roms only ever operates on arcade systems (prompt_for_systems with arcade_only=true selects find_arcade_systems), resolves the target strategy from -m/--merging or an interactive select, and runs rebuild_system once per selected system; it has no GraphQL mutation, unlike generate-playlists.

rebuild_system runs a repair pass before comparing merging strategies: for every Partial game it takes roms with romfile_id IS NULL (skipping size 0), searches the same system for a romfile with the same size and CRC, then MD5, then SHA1, and re-imports the found file through import_roms::import_other constrained to that single game id with UnattendedMode::Skip. Consequently a rebuild with an unchanged strategy still heals unlinked roms before printing Nothing to do.

The rebuild migration direction is chosen by a two-branch test on (stored, target): Split/NonMerged -> NonMerged/FullNonMerged expands, NonMerged/FullNonMerged -> Split/NonMerged trims, any other pair only re-records systems.merging; both branches iterate find_full_games_by_system_id so Partial games are never expanded or trimmed, and --force bypasses the unchanged-strategy early return.

expand_game defines each strategy by the rom set it demands: NonMerged uses find_roms_by_game_id_parents_no_parent_bioses (own roms plus merged roms whose parent rom is not bios), FullNonMerged uses find_roms_by_game_id_parents (every rom including BIOS dependencies), and roms flagged disk are dropped from either set.

add_rom materializes an expanded rom in one of four ways depending on source/destination layout (archive->archive via archive::copy_files_between_archives raw copy with rename, file->archive via to_archive plus rename_file, archive->file via extract+rename+create, file->file via copy+create) and always finishes by pointing the clone's rom at the destination romfile, leaving the parent's file untouched.

If a merged rom's parent has no file, expand_game prints Missing "<rom>" and returns Ok(()) from inside the open transaction without committing, so that game's partial expansion is rolled back while the rebuild continues with the next game rather than failing.

trim_game releases files rather than creating them: under Split it deletes every rom with a parent_id, under NonMerged only the BIOS-flagged merged roms, deletes each from the set's archive or disk, sets romfile_id = NULL, and updates the archive romfile row size; ArchiveFile::delete_file additionally deletes the archive itself once it becomes empty.

The merging transition matrix is pinned by five in-module tests under src/rebuild_roms (test_nothing_to_do, test_split_to_non_merged, test_split_to_full_non_merged, test_non_merged_to_split, test_full_non_merged_to_non_merged), all driven by the MAME Rebuild fixture through the real subcommand matches.

generate-playlists is scoped to Redump systems via prompt_for_systems(connection, Some(REDUMP_SYSTEM_URL), ...), and the GraphQL generatePlaylists mutation always invokes it with -a so every Redump system is processed at once.

Multi-disc grouping is defined solely by DISC_REGEX = r" \(Disc \d+\).*": games whose name matches are grouped under the regex-stripped name plus .m3u, and because the trailing .* consumes everything after the disc marker, differing suffixes on the same title still collapse into one playlist. src/common.rs reuses the same regex to derive the playlist path, keeping generated and sorted names identical.

process_system skips a whole disc group when any member game is not Completion::Full, and picks only the first non-empty romfile bucket among chd, cso, cue, iso, rvz, so mixed-format sets yield a playlist for one format and incomplete sets leave playlist_id NULL.
An M3U is written next to the first matching romfile of the group (set_file_name on that romfile's absolute path) and contains only bare filenames, one per line with a trailing newline.

Playlist persistence checks find_romfile_by_path with the absolute path while Persist::create stores the ROM-directory-relative path, so for rows stored after the relative-path migration the update/dedupe branch never matches and a re-run inserts rather than updates the playlist row.

generate-playlists ends each group by setting games.playlist_id for every member game; the column is an INTEGER REFERENCES romfiles(id) ON DELETE SET NULL with an index, so a playlist is an ordinary typed romfiles row whose deletion only unlinks discs.

The CHD parents feature resolves a disc's parent image from games.playlist_id: find_parent_chd_romfile_by_game takes the first game ordered by name in that playlist and its .chd romfile, returning None when playlist_id is NULL. to_chd therefore writes romfiles.parent_id only for systems whose playlists were generated first, and sorts games so children are converted before parents.

CHD_PARENTS is a per-system boolean setting defaulting to false read with get_bool(..., Some(system.id)); convert-roms --parents bypasses it in favor of an interactive prompt_for_parent_romfile ranked by Jaro-Winkler similarity, while export-roms calls find_parent_chd_romfile_by_game unconditionally.

sort-roms treats playlists as movable romfiles: sort_system preloads find_playlist_romfiles_by_system_id into its romfile map and sort_game queues a move for game.playlist_id whenever its path differs from Game::get_playlist_path, which honours the 1G1R directory and the REGIONS_*_SUBFOLDERS alpha scheme; test_sort_1g1r_playlist asserts the M3U ends up under system_directory/1G1R alongside the discs.
Playlist rows are protected from cleanup: find_orphan_romfiles excludes any romfile referenced by games.playlist_id, so purge-roms --orphan cannot delete an M3U that has no roms pointing at it.

Arcade sets are stored one directory per game unless the extension is an archive (system.arcade && !ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS in get_sorted_path), which is why expand_game and trim_game both target <system_directory>/<game_name>/ and resolve <game_name>.zip as the alternative archive layout.
rebuild-roms declares -y/--yes but never reads it (unlike sort-roms and purge-roms which read matches.get_flag("YES")), because the rebuild path performs no confirmation prompt; the flag is a no-op.

generate-playlists is not re-run automatically after format conversion: sort-roms relocates playlists with the games, but after convert-roms the command must be run again to reflect new filenames, and a rebuild only touches roms of games that are Full under the currently stored strategy, so incomplete BIOS sets leave clones Partial until a second rebuild.
